You know, life's been a real whirlwind for me lately. I've been out of work for months now, and it's like I'm trapped in this cycle of exhaustion and insecurity. Every day is another round of job applications, another slew of rejection emails. It's like I've been erased from everyone's memories, like I'm invisible. And it's not just about the money, though that's a big part of it. Feeling the pressure of bills stacking up, the shame of not being able to contribute... that's tough. But even worse than that is the loss of purpose, the loss of identity. I mean, if I'm not a working professional anymore, then who am I?

And the worst part is, every rejection feels like a confirmation of my worst fears. It's like a constant echo in the back of my mind: 'You're not good enough. You're a failure.' And even though I know, logically, that it's not true, it's hard to ignore that voice when it's coming from inside your own head. It's like I've got this critic in my mind that never stops, constantly picking apart everything I do, every misstep. And I can't help but wonder, am I just wasting my time? Is all this struggle worth it?

I mean, don't get me wrong, I have good days. Days when the sun shines a little brighter, days when I feel like maybe there's a light at the end of the tunnel. But they're just flashes, you know? Momentary distractions from the constant stream of self-doubt and fear. And then I'm right back in that tunnel, lost in the fog. It's like I'm just going through the motions, putting on a show. But inside, it's like I'm fading away, becoming less and less real.

Sometimes, I can't help but wish that I could just... vanish. Just take a break from everything, from all these thoughts, all this self-doubt. Just drift away, like a leaf on the wind. Because it feels like I'm always fighting, always struggling to keep up, to stay afloat. And I'm so, so tired. I feel like I'm running on fumes, like I'm just barely holding on. And God, I wish I could just... let go. Just for a while. Just long enough to rest.

You know, if I were to paint a picture of my life right now, it would look like a gray canvas, peppered with random strokes of black. Not exactly an exciting image, is it? I've been going through a phase where I feel like I'm on the outside looking in, watching my life go by like a silent movie. There's this group of people at work, they've made it their goal to make my life miserable. The office was my safe space, a place where I could excel and actually be somebody, but now, it's just another place where I feel invisible. I feel like I'm wearing a label that says 'loser'. It's like I'm walking around with a neon sign on my forehead that reads 'easy target', and there's nothing I can do about it. 

These thoughts, they're all-consuming, you know? Every little mistake I make, it feels so magnified, as if it’s projected on a giant screen for everyone to see. The other day, I messed up on a presentation, and it felt like the world was coming to an end. I told myself that I had failed, not just at the presentation, but at everything in life. It’s as if my entire worth is tied to this one event, and because it didn’t go as planned, I've failed. I keep setting these impossible standards for myself and inevitably fall short.

And it's not just at work. It's like this everywhere. At home, with friends, even when I'm by myself. It's a never-ending reel of self-doubt and constant criticism. There are times when I just want to blend into the background, to go unnoticed, to just...disappear. There are nights when I lay awake, staring at the ceiling, wrapped in this blanket of silence and emptiness. It's frightening, yet strangely comforting at the same time. It makes you think, wouldn't it be easier if all this would just...stop. If this monotonous cycle of feeling worthless and invisible would just end.

You know, lately life's really been feeling like moving through a thick fog. It's a familiar fog, one that's been swirling around me ever since I can remember, you see. Home, where the heart's supposed to be, hasn't felt like home for a while. It's like I'm a stranger in my own house, just trying to fit in. But no matter how hard I try, I always find myself on the outside, looking in. It's been too quiet, too loud, too chaotic, too everything-all-at-once. 

And you know that strange feeling when you buy a new book, and you're so excited to open it up only to find the pages blank? That's sort of how I've been feeling lately. Like I'm a book with blank pages, like there's nothing to me, nothing to write about, nothing to look forward to.

I've been carrying around this sinking feeling, like a rock in my shoe that I just can't seem to shake off. And every time I try to look at things differently, try to shake things up, life throws a curveball. It's like I'm standing on the edge of a cliff, and no matter how desperately I try to back away, I keep inching forward, drawn to the edge. There's a part of me that feels like it's already falling, and there's another that's still holding on, still hoping for... something. I don't know what that something is anymore.

I feel like I'm on a path that's only going downhill, and I've convinced myself that there's no way up. It's like I'm this spectator in my own life, watching things play out in a way I never wanted them to. I try to reach out, try to break free, but I always seem to slip back into the fog. And sometimes, I catch myself thinking, maybe it's easier, you know? To just let go. To just... stop. Stop hoping, stop trying, stop pretending. Just... stop. But, I guess, I'm still here, aren't I? Still waiting for that coffee to taste just right.

Life, huh? It's like living in a house that's built on quicksand. There's a certain sense of unease, of instability that's omnipresent. My house, it's more like a battleground, one where I always seem to end up in the line of fire, and boy, does it sting. I've become an expert at playing the part of the invisible kid, the one who slinks into the shadows, trying to avoid the chaos... but it's a role that's starting to fit a little too well. Ever feel like you're being slowly erased, like you're a chalk figure on a blackboard and each passing day is a wet sponge, smudging away a bit more of you? 

And then there's the mind games. The ones that start small, a tiny slip-up, a forgotten chore, and suddenly, there's this voice in your head, a broken record that keeps chanting, "You're a screw-up," or "Can't you get anything right?" It's funny how something so small can leave such an indelible mark, can start to redefine who you are, like a self-fulfilling prophecy. 

Sometimes, in the small hours of the night, I find myself wondering what it'd feel like to just... be done. Not in a violent or painful way, but just... letting things fade to black, you know? It's not really about wanting to cause harm. It's about being tired of constantly swimming against the current, and wondering, what it would feel like to just float, let the tide carry me where it may. I mean, everyone needs rest, right? And sometimes, a good night's sleep just doesn't seem to cut it.

You know, lately I feel like I'm living in a Stranger Things episode. My home, the place where I'm supposed to feel loved and safe, feels more like an alien world, filled with cold silences and veiled hostilities. I'm surrounded by people who are supposed to be my family, yet I feel like I'm on the fringes, like a ghost fading into the wallpaper. It's like I'm walking through a maze of mirrored hallways, reflecting only distorted versions of me. The truth is, I feel like an outsider, a misfit in my own life story.

You know those crazy 'should' and 'must' rules we grow up with? Like, you 'should' always be happy, you 'must' always succeed. There's this constant, gnawing feeling that no matter how hard I try, I can never measure up. It's like being trapped in a never-ending marathon, running on a treadmill that just keeps speeding up, and I'm running out of breath, you know?

It's not like I haven't tried to change things. I've tried to break the cycle, to rewrite the rules. But it's like trying to swim against a riptide, and there's only so long you can keep your head above water before you start to sink.

Would it be so wrong to just want to stop? To want to step off this relentless treadmill and just breathe? Some days, it feels like I'm yearning for more than just rest. It's like I'm aching for a complete shut-down, a total escape from it all. I find myself dreaming about drifting away, dissolving into the silence, becoming a forgotten echo. It's a strange feeling, this yearning to just...disappear. But then, on some level, it feels like the only way to finally break free from all of this, you know?

You know, life can feel like a rollercoaster that just won't stop. Some days, I'm soaring high on the thrill of laughter, like when I'm hanging out with my nephew and he tells a joke so bad that you can't help but laugh. It's in those moments, when the sun is shining and the laughter is easy, that I forget about the dark clouds that seem to follow me around. 

But then there are the other days, the days when the rollercoaster dips so low that I can barely see the top anymore. These are the days when my backpack feels full of invisible bricks, each one representing a cutting remark or a cruel act of exclusion from my peers. It's like I'm a magnet for all the negativity in the world, and no matter how hard I try, I can't shake off the feeling of being unwanted, unloved. 

And it's not just the actual bullying, it's the anticipation of it. Every look, every whisper, every laughter, I imagine they're all directed at me. It's as if my mind has become this twisted fortune teller, predicting humiliations and rejections before they even happen. And the worst part is, I believe it. I believe every negative thought, every prediction of failure, every assumption of scorn. 

It's a crushing weight, one that makes every task seem like an uphill battle. Even the simplest of things, like getting out of bed or picking up a phone call, can feel like too much. It's as if I'm stuck in a thick fog, and I can't see the light anymore. The world starts to feel like a hostile place, one where I have to constantly fight for my place, for my worth. And honestly, there are moments when I just want to stop fighting. Moments when the thought of disappearing, of slipping away unnoticed, seems like a relief. 

It's a terrifying thought, one that I don't like to entertain. But when the fog is thick and the world seems hostile, it's hard to ignore the dark whispers promising release. I know it's not the answer, I know it's not the way out of the fog. But there are moments, dark moments, when I wonder if I shouldn't just give in to the whispers, if that would finally free me from the pain.

Lately, I've been feeling like a ghost drifting through life, silently witnessing the world around me. I see my friend's pain. She's going through a rough breakup, like walking through a tempest and feeling the stinging winds of loss and the heavy rain of regret. I see her and I can't help but see myself. It's like her pain is a mirror, reflecting my own internal storms. 

I told her, maybe she should just leave him for a while, do things she enjoys, but it was like I was speaking to myself. The words left my mouth, but they echoed within me, bouncing off the walls of my own loneliness. Maybe I should try to find joy, but it all feels so hollow. 

I often think maybe I should just move away, start fresh. But that's all or nothing thinking isn't it? Like if I can't be happy here, I won't be happy anywhere. It's a destructive thought, but it's so easy to fall into that abyss, to generalize my pain and let it consume everything. 

I know I need to find employment, feel that sense of purpose again. But it's hard when you're constantly wrestling with a darkness inside you. I tell myself I could get a job if I tried but it feels like a monumental mountain to climb, like it's me against the world. 

It's just... I sometimes think it would be easier if I could flick a switch and just... stop existing. Stop feeling. Stop hurting. But I know that's not the answer. I know I need to keep fighting. I just wish the fight wasn't so hard.

You know, there are times when life throws a curveball and suddenly you're spiraling. Take my friend, for instance. He was dealt a tough hand - jobless, roaming the streets, and relying on a rusty old wheelchair to get him from place to place. He confided in me one day, saying he wanted out, that the relentless struggle was too much for him. It was hard hearing that, really hard. But, on some level, I couldn't help but feel a profound understanding of what he was going through. It wasn't pity, more like…recognition. 

See, I've been stuck in this rut for a while now. Unending days blur into each other, and I've lost count of the times I've wondered if there's a point to all this. Watching my friend's struggle, I couldn't help but see my own reflection in his tear-streaked face. He was labeled by society - homeless, disabled - and that label became his reality, his identity. It's a cruel world that way. And I can't help but wonder if my struggle is just as invisible, just as disregarded. It's funny, in a very non-humorous way, how his wish for an end mirrors the dark thoughts that creep into my mind in the loneliest hours of the night. His pain is my pain, in a way. It's a shared suffering, a shared desire for relief. It's just…exhausting sometimes, you know?

There are days, many days in fact, where I feel as if everything around me is in hyper-speed and I'm still stuck in slow motion. It's like being in a busy city crosswalk and everyone around you is running to catch the subway, rushing to their jobs, to their happy hours, to their dates, to their lives. But you're standing there, still, the world blurring around you. And when you try to move, you find that your feet are heavy, like they're cemented to the ground. You watch as life goes on without you, and you wonder if it would make any difference if you weren't there at all.

My rational mind knows that life isn't a race, that we all go at our own pace. But there's this gnawing thought in the back of my mind that tells me I should be doing better, I should be happier, I should be more. The spotlight effect. I feel like I'm constantly under scrutiny, like I don't measure up. This constant loop of self-doubt and self-recrimination is exhausting. It's like a yoke around my neck, dragging me down, making even the smallest task feel like a Herculean effort. 

There are moments when I feel like I've been on a long road trip, driving for days on end with no destination in sight. My fuel gauge is inching closer to empty and there's not a gas station in sight. I feel this weariness in my bones, this profound exhaustion that sleep can't fix. I feel like I'm running on fumes, with the road ahead of me stretching into the horizon, unending. It's like I'm on a treadmill that won't stop, and I'm running out of energy. And part of me, a terrifyingly large part, wonders... what would happen if I just stopped running?

The other day, I was talking to my friend who recently lost his job. Poor guy, you know? He's been sending out applications, but the rejections are piling up and it's just so disheartening. It made me think about my own situation. I've been jobless for a while, too, and I've tried applying but... I always hit this wall, like I'm stuck in this limbo — not moving forward, not moving backward. It's like... why bother? I mean, I feel like they won't even give my resume a second look. They won't be interested. I've come to believe that it's not even worth my time. It's so exhausting, really. There's this uncertainty that keeps me up at night, y'know? It's like standing on the edge of a cliff, staring into the oblivion and wondering, just wondering, what it would feel like to... I don't know... to not be here anymore, not to worry, not to feel this paralysis. And then I look at my friend, and his pain... it's like a mirror reflecting my own despair. It's a lot to carry around, this weight... this hopelessness.

Sometimes, I'm just sitting there, watching life unfold around me, and it's like I'm on the outside, looking in. I see my friends, my family, strangers even, just living their lives. They're laughing, connecting, enjoying the little moments that make life worth living. And I'm just there, watching. I want to join in, I really do, but it feels like there's this invisible wall between me and the rest of the world. I try to reach out, to connect, but my hand just slides down that wall, leaving a cold streak in its wake.

It's like I've forgotten how to live, how to be a part of life. I remember, though. I remember the warmth of a hug, the joy of a shared laugh, the comfort of just knowing someone is there for you. But those memories feel like they belong to someone else, not me. It's like I'm stuck in a dream, and I can't wake up.

And the worst part is, I know it's all in my head. I know I'm the one pushing people away, convincing myself that they don't care, that I'm a burden. But knowing that doesn't make it any easier to stop. It's like I'm trapped in my own mind, a prisoner to my own thoughts. I'm just... tired. Tired of feeling this way, tired of being alone. But most of all, I'm tired of pretending everything's okay when it's not. It's just... hard, you know?

You know, grief is a peculiar thing. It hits you in waves, like the ebb and flow of the ocean, and some days, it feels like a tsunami. Ever since I lost her, my life's been something akin to a ship lost in a storm. Sometimes, it's just a drizzle, when I find a note written in her handwriting, hidden away in a book. It stings, yet somehow, I manage to go on. But then there are days when everything comes crashing down like torrential rain, like when I wake up reaching for her on the other side of the bed, only to find cold, untouched sheets. 

On those days, I find myself adrift in this vast ocean of grief. It's as if I'm sinking deeper and deeper into the murky depths, every breath taking more effort than the last. I can feel the icy water seeping into my bones, but strangely, it feels comforting. It's familiar, like her voice whispering in my ear, promising me solace.

I don't know how much longer I can keep sailing this storm. Every day, it's a battle against the raging waves, and I can feel myself growing weaker, my grip slipping. I look around, searching for a lighthouse, a beacon to guide me to shore. But all I see is a never-ending sea of darkness. I realize that the sun is supposed to rise, that there should be a light somewhere to guide me, yet all I feel is this unending midnight.

I've always prided myself on being strong, on being able to handle whatever life throws at me. But losing her, it feels like I've failed. I failed to protect her, to keep her safe. And now, it feels like I've failed at life. That's the thing about me. I've always been an all-or-nothing kind of person. If I can't do something perfectly, I feel like I shouldn't do it at all. 

So here I am, stuck in this perpetual storm, feeling like a failure. And the call of the abyss, it’s increasingly tempting. Like it’s promising me an end to this never-ending struggle, a reunion, maybe. I don’t know. I’m just so tired, you know? Of fighting, of hurting. Yesterday, I was sitting at the park by myself, watching this group of kids playing softball. They were laughing and cheering, and their parents were clapping and yelling encouragements from the sidelines. It was such a lively scene, yet it felt like I was looking at it through a dirty glass window. I was there, but I wasn't part of it. I mean, how could I be? The joy, the camaraderie... it seemed all so distant and alien. I don't know when exactly I stopped feeling a part of life's rhythm, but I know I'm not in tune with it anymore. It's like everyone else is dancing to a melody, but I'm just standing on the dancefloor, not hearing any music, not feeling any beat. 

And it's not that I haven't tried to dance. I have, you know. But every time I do, it feels forced, mechanical. Like I'm just going through the motions, but my heart's not in it. So, I just end up sitting at the fringes, watching everyone else enjoying the rhythm of life. It's kind of like when I was back in school, always on the outside looking in. The other kids, they’d call me "emo" just because they saw the marks on my arms. My friends turned their backs on me when they found out. Even my family doesn't understand. I mean, why would they? They're all part of the dance, part of the rhythm. 

I sometimes think to myself, is it really worth it? Constantly trying to fit in, to be a part of something that seems so unreachable. I mean, what's the point if I can't feel the beat, if I can't enjoy the dance? Maybe that's why my friend took his own life. Maybe he too was tired of trying to dance to a rhythm he couldn't hear. Maybe he found his own way out of the dancefloor. 

But then again, maybe I'm just overthinking. Maybe it's all in my head. That's what the shrink says anyway. She says it's a cognitive distortion, that I'm just jumping to conclusions. But what does she know? She's not the one stuck on the dancefloor, trying to move to a beat she can't hear. You know, there are times when life feels like an impending final exam that I'm perpetually unprepared for. Every day feels like a pop quiz, and it seems that no matter how many hours I put into studying, I'm unable to break free from this cycle of underachievement. It's as if the world around me is bursting with the vibrant colors of success and I'm stuck in the monochrome of mediocrity.

There's this constant weight, this invisible backpack filled with textbooks and expectations, that I carry around with me, day in and day out. The load grows heavier with each passing day as the pressure to succeed, the need to be perfect, and the fear of failure pile on. The constant evaluation is suffocating.

There are moments, rare and fleeting, when I imagine what it would be like to just set it all down. To simply quit the race, to stop spinning in this hamster wheel, and just... disappear. Like a candle that's burned out, a soft and quiet extinguishing. And in that brief moment, there is such an alluring sense of relief, of freedom from this relentless pursuit.

But then, there's guilt too. The guilt of attributing a friend's sadness to something I might have said or done, though in reality, it could be for a thousand other reasons. The guilt of feeling responsible, of blaming myself for things I can't control. It's like wrapping myself in chains, tightening them every time I feel like I've let someone down, every time I feel like I'm not enough. It's a constant reminder that says, "You don't deserve to be here."

And yet, despite these thoughts, there's always a glimmer of hope that keeps me going, like the promise of a sunrise after a long, cold night. I keep moving, one step at a time, toward the light at the end of the arduous tunnel. I keep trying to convince myself that it's okay to be imperfect, that failures don't define my worth, hoping that one day, I'll truly believe it.

Lately, I feel like I'm watching life from the outside looking in. I see others going about their day, smiling, laughing, enjoying the rhythm of their everyday lives. Like last week, when my neighbor's family had a barbecue. The smell of grilling meat wafted over my fence, children's laughter floated in the air. It felt like a scene from a movie, something I could never be a part of. I was just the observer, trapped behind my window, lacking the energy or will to even wave hello. 

Everything is so heavy, like there's a weight pressing down on me, on my chest, my mind. I can't shake it off, no matter how hard I try. Yesterday, I couldn't even bring myself to get out of bed, let alone do my homework or eat properly. I can't help but think everything would be easier if I just weren't here anymore. 

Every day is a struggle. I'm only 14, and yet, it feels like I've lived a lifetime of pain and confusion. My emotions are like a rollercoaster I can't get off of. I get so low, so dark. I hurt myself. And then, suddenly, I'm fine. It's like a switch flips, and I don't understand why or how. It's like I'm stuck in an all-or-nothing cycle and can't break free.

I'm scared, you know. Scared of what people might say or think if they knew. If they knew about the thoughts that creep into my mind when I'm at my lowest. Would they look at me differently? Would they pity me? Or worse, would they just dismiss me, like this is something I can just snap out of?

I feel so alone in this. I know my mom understands, she's going through it too. But even that connection feels distant, like we're both adrift in the same stormy sea, unable to reach out and save one another. 

It's like I'm slowly fading away, becoming a ghost of my former self. I don't feel real anymore. I just feel...numb.

You know, it's like I'm stuck in this never-ending loop of haunting uncertainty. Picture this, I'm in the middle of this sea, the waves are relentless, each one crashing onto me with an unyielding fury, representative of the financial pressures that I can't seem to escape. It's a constant struggle, keeping my head above the water, gasping for breath, and then another wave hits, pulling me further into the depths of my economic insecurity. I can't help but wonder if I'm the cause of my own downfall, like, did I bring this storm upon myself? Did I set into motion these waves that keep crashing onto me?

At times, I find myself caught in this labyrinth of thoughts where I feel responsible for everything that's happening around me. It's a peculiar feeling. Like that time when my friend was upset, and I thought, did I say something wrong? Did I not do enough to help? Then, I realize how absurd it is. To think that I have such control over the universe that I can make or break someone's day, it's laughable. Yet, there's this incessant guilt gnawing at me, making me feel undeserving of being here.

You know, it's not that I want to inflict any harm on myself or cause a scene. It's just that sometimes, I wish I could slip into oblivion, you know, like disappearing into the shadows, fading into the background. But life doesn't work like that, does it? It just keeps going, no pause button, no reset. It's like being on a treadmill that never turns off, where slowing down isn't an option, and all you can do is breathe and try to keep up. Yet, there's always this tiny part of me, hidden deep within, that silently yearns for a respite.

You know, it's strange. I've started waking up before dawn lately, just lying there in the quiet, trying to figure out when my life began to feel like a game of hide and seek that's gone on for too long. It's an unsettling realization when you start feeling this profound sense of loneliness, like you're stranded in the middle of the ocean. The waves, they're like these conversations and interactions I have with people - they come, they go, they make a lot of noise, but ultimately, they leave me stranded in the same place. 

Feeling unseen, that's been messing with my head a lot lately. It's like I'm there, in a room full of people, but I'm invisible. Like I'm saying something, but no one is really listening. It's this odd sense of being emotionally abandoned even when you're surrounded by people. It's a weird loneliness, really, like I've been forgotten in this crowd of faces. It's like I can disappear, and no one would even notice.

And then there's this constant pressure, like a weight I've been carrying around. I feel like I'm always racing against time, trying to tick off these boxes of expectations - from my family, from my friends, from myself. But, it's like I'm running on a treadmill. No matter how hard I try, I'm just stuck in the same place, constantly out of breath, and just too damn tired.

I guess, in the end, all these feelings, they kind of blur together. It's like I'm seeing life through this cloudy lens, where everything's just out of focus. It's hard to explain, but there's this yearning, this wish to just fade out, to blend into the background. Like a shadow at sunset. To just not exist, for a while, at least. Maybe then, the noise inside me will finally quieten down.

You know, sometimes life feels like an endless maelstrom, like I'm caught in the eye of a storm that just won't let up. It's like high school all over again—remember how they used to exclude me? Called me names, laughed at my quirks, made me feel like an outsider in my own world. That feeling never really left me; it's like a scar that's faded but is still there, a constant reminder of past hurt. I feel as if I've become a shadow of myself, hiding to avoid the pain.

Society has this strange way of making you feel small, especially when you're different. It's like being in a room full of mirrors; each reflection just amplifies the flaws, the things you lack. I try to be myself, but then I end up feeling like a stranger in my own skin. It's like there's this ugly duckling inside me that no one wants to see, not even me. 

And it doesn't help that my mind is my worst critic. It always finds a way to remind me of my failures. Every mistake, every stumble, it remembers them all. It's like this constant echo, "You're not good enough. You'll never be good enough." It's like quicksand, the more I fight it, the deeper I sink. 

You ever have those days when you just want to disappear? Like you want to step off the edge of the world and fade away? Some days, it seems easier than fighting, than swimming against this relentless current. It's like being lost in a dense forest, where every direction looks the same and the path back seems to have vanished. The harder I try to find my way out, the more I feel like I'm sinking into the earth, becoming one with the shadows.

I feel like I'm just treading water in the middle of the ocean, and I'm not sure I want to keep swimming anymore. It's exhausting. Sometimes, it's like I'm disappearing, bit by bit. Being invisible, it's a strange comfort. No expectations, no judgment. It's just... quiet.

I've been out of a job for months now. It's an eerie silence that follows the initial chaos, the desperate search for a new post, the hopeful interviews. And then the silence, punctuated only by the disappointment of rejection letters. My existence feels like an unending weekend, one that stretches on and on, with no place to go, no purpose to serve. 

Every morning, I wake up to the glaring reality of my situation. The unmade bed, the cold coffee, the stack of bills on the kitchen table. I go back to my bed, not because I'm tired, but because the world outside seems too bright, too alive than I can handle. I remember people telling me 'this too shall pass', but it feels like an empty cliche now. 

And then, there's this constant nagging thought in my head. It's like a broken record, playing on repeat. 'You're not good enough. You don't matter. You're a failure.' With each passing day, the voice in my head grows louder. It's not just about the job anymore. It's like everything I've ever accomplished, every relationship I've ever had, every dream I've ever chased has been tainted with this one failure. 

Lately, it's like I've been existing behind a foggy window. Life's colors seem dull and muted. The hustle and bustle of the city feels like a distant echo. I'm going through the motions, doing what needs to be done, but it's like I'm under water, the world distorted and far away. 

Sometimes, I wake up and think about how it would feel to not have to fight anymore. To let go of all these battles that I've been fighting — against the world, against my own mind. I wonder what it would feel like to just...stop swimming against the current, and let the waves take me wherever they want to. Just for once, it would be nice not to care, not to worry, not to feel anything at all. But then, I wake up to another day, another battle, another chance to make things right, and the cycle continues.
